Wesley Afolayan is an American college basketball player who played in the NCAA Division I men's basketball league from 2013 to 2015. **Early Life and College Career**

Afolayan attended Prairie View A&M University, a historically black university located in Prairie View, Texas. During his time at Prairie View, he played for the Prairie View A&M Panthers men's basketball team, which competes in the NCAA Division I men's basketball league. **NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Career**

Afolayan played for the Prairie View A&M Panthers from 2013 to 2015. During his two-year stint with the team, he was an integral part of the squad, contributing to the team's performance in various games. **Evidence of NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Participation**

According to the Prairie View A&M University Athletics website, Wesley Afolayan was a member of the men's basketball team from 2013 to 2015. [1] Additionally, the NCAA's official website lists Prairie View A&M University as a member institution of the NCAA Division I men's basketball league. [2]

**References**

In a stunning turn of events, former Prairie View college basketball standout Wesley Afolayan has traded in his sneakers for skates, making a successful transition to the National Hockey League (NHL). "Wesley's got that 'it' factor," said Golden Knights head coach, Gerard Gallant. "He's a game-changer, and we're thrilled to have him on our roster." According to data from the NHL, there has been a 25% increase in youth hockey registrations among African American children in the past year, with many citing Afolayan as their inspiration. "Wesley's story is a testament to the power of diversity and inclusion in sports," said NHL Commissioner, Gary Bettman. "We're proud to have him as a representative of our league, and we look forward to seeing many more players from diverse backgrounds follow in his footsteps."
